For the Petitioner : Mr. Shree Niwas Roy, Advocate For the State : Mr. Arwind Kumar, A.P.P. .....
Order No.10/ Dated:15.04.2024
1.

The instant criminal revision is directed against judgment dated 27.05.2016 passed by learned Principal District & Additional Sessions Judge-II, Giridih in Cr. Appeal No. 36 of 2014 whereby and whereunder the appeal preferred by the petitioner has been dismissed and the Judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 23.07.2014 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Giridih in T.R. No. 649 of 2014 arising out of Hirodih P.S. Case No. 44/2010 dated 21.08.2010 corresponding to G.R. No. 1879 of 2010 sentence to undergo RI for three years and a fine of Rs. 5000/- under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code and in case of default of payment of fine the petitioner shall further undergo RI for six months, has been affirmed.
2.

entities.text: Principal District & Additional Sessions Judge-II, Giridih
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Factual matrix of this case is that marriage of the informant was solemnized with the petitioner Manowar Hussain in the year 2005 and was given cash, ornaments, a motorcycle and several other articles.

It is alleged that at the time of marriage the petitioner has demanded Rs. 50,000/- cash which was refused by Idrish Mian, the father of the informant but after some time they started torturing the informant due to non-fulfillment of the said demand.

It has further been alleged that on 22.07.2010 all the accused persons by hatching criminal conspiracy caught hold of the informant and tried to kill her and on raising alarm, neighbors gathered there and her life was saved.
It has further been alleged that she was driven out from the matrimonial house by the accused persons at night and she was not even allowed to see her minor child.
3. After completion of investigation, charge-sheet was submitted against the present petitioner for the offences under Sections 498A of the I.P.C.
Cognizance against the petitioner on the basis of charge sheet was taken on 22.09.2011 for the offence under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
Charges were framed on 12.06.2012 under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text:
After trial, the petitioner was convicted for the offence under Sections 498A of the I.P.C. with sentences as stated above, which was assailed in the Criminal Appeal No.36/2014, which was dismissed and conviction and sentence of the petitioner was affirmed by the appellate court, which has been assailed in this revision.
4.

Both the parties have appeared in person at the time of hearing of this revision petition and a joint compromise petition in the shape of I.A. No. 10292/2023 has been filed, which is not disputed by the opposite party No. 2 (wife)/informant of this case.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that both the parties have settled their dispute outside the Court and are residing together and are discharging their conjugal obligations with each other.

In the aforementioned factual background and change of circumstances, it is argued that without going into the merits of judgment of conviction, the petitioner may be released on probation under Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, which shall meet the ends of justice in this case.

6. On the other hand, learned Addl.P.P. for State assisted by learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 have raised no objection against the above contention regarding release of petitioner on probation bond.

7. Both parties have compromised their issues and are living together since six years back just after filing of this revision application and I.A. No. 10292/2023 has been filed showing joint compromise between the parties.
8.
Both parties have physically appeared before this Court and also admit the factum of compromise and living together since six to seven years ago.
9. Under such circumstances, sending the petitioner again back for undergoing imprisonment would not meet the ends of justice.

Therefore, it would be an appropriate to release the petitioner under Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 instead of awarding substantive sentence of imprisonment as awarded by learned trial court and confirmed by appellate court.

10. Accordingly, impugned Judgment/Order are hereby modified to the extent that instead of awarding substantive sentence of imprisonment, the petitioner is directed to be released on furnishing bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten Thousand) along with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of learned trial court with condition that he shall maintain peace and good behavior with his wife and children and maintain peace in the society.

11. In case of violation of terms and conditions of the bond, petitioner shall be called upon by the concerned trial court for sustaining the remaining period of imprisonment as awarded by the concerned trial court within a period of three years.

sentences.text: Petitioner shall appear once at the interval of two months before the probation officer who shall watch the conduct of the petitioner and report to the trial court.

13. However, the complainant shall be at liberty to file an application before the concerned trial court for serving the rest of the sentence, if the petitioner deliberately violates the conditions of bond.

If the petitioner wants to change his fixed abode within the above said period of three years,
the same shall also be reported before the concerned trial court with the consent of the complainant.
14. In view of above discussions and reasons, the conviction of petitioner is maintained with modification in the sentence.
15. Petitioner is further directed to furnish the bond under Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 as stated above within three months from the date of this order.
16. Accordingly, this criminal revision petition is disposed of.

17. Let the copy of this order along with record of trial court be sent immediately for information and needful to the concerned court.
18.
I.A. No. 10292 of 2023 stands allowed.
